Think of the song that gives you goosebumps. Your brain thinks it's a threat.
Your brain always guesses what comes next in a song.
Then, surprise! A key change. A new instrument. A huge build-up.

text: Scientists think a fast alarm in your brain asks: danger?

Your body reacts like you're scared. Tiny muscles pull every hair up. Goosebumps.
A leftover from hairy ancestors: puffed-up hair looked bigger.

text: Then a slower part checks. It's just a song. Relief.

Brain scans at McGill University showed dopamine, a feel-good chemical, at the chill moment.
And even in the seconds before, while you wait for it.

text: Scared and rewarded at once. Do you get them? Yes or no?
